newsitem.title: INDIA: WTO seeks regional pacts on competition policy.
newsitem.headline: WTO seeks regional pacts on competition policy.

text.p: A senior World Trade Organization (WTO) official said on Monday that trading nations must strive for bilateral and regional cooperation on competition policy until a multilateral agreement was reached.

"As we proceed towards the goal (multilateral cooperation), much can be achieved by pursuing at the same time bilateral and regional cooperation on competition policy," Anwarul Hoda, deputy director-general of WTO, told a business conference.
"The search for multilateral cooperation in competition policy will be long and arduous and face many challenges," he said.

A ministerial meeting of the WTO at Singapore in December decided to set up a working group to study issues relating to interaction between trade and competition policy, including anti-competitive practices.
No time frame has been fixed for the working group to give its final recommendations.
"It depends on how ambitious the governments become," Hoda said in reply to a question on the time frame during which the working group would conclude its study.
"Competition policies, or lack of them, or deficiencies in their enforcement have emerged as a source of tension in international trade and economic relations," Hoda said.
There was also some disagreement among WTO members on anti-dumping policies, he added.
Anti-dumping policies concern measures undertaken by nations against the selling of products in their markets by foreign compeititors at below-cost prices.
"Some members have suggested that anti-dumping policy should be replaced by competition policy," Hoda said.
"Other members, however, do not agree..." he said.
